planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once frost danger has passed; Candyland Red is a 2020 All-America Selections winner currant tomato bred for a prolific, intensely sweet harvest of tiny fruit on a tall indeterminate vine.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed, staking or caging the tall indeterminate vine for support. Candyland Red, a 2020 All-America Selections winner, is a currant-type tomato producing an enormous quantity of tiny, intensely sweet, deep red fruit in loose clusters continuously from midsummer until frost, offering some of the highest sugar content of any tomato type for snacking straight off the vine. The vigorous vine benefits from regular watering and feeding to sustain its heavy, continuous fruit set through the Gulf South growing season. Harvest clusters as fruit ripens to full red color, and expect the plant to keep producing right up until cold weather ends the season.

common_name: Cabernet Eggplant (AAS-Winning Glossy Purple-Black Hybrid Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once soil and air have warmed well past frost danger; Cabernet is a 2006 All-America Selections winner hybrid eggplant bred for vigor, high yield, and classic glossy purple-black fruit.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 60°F. Cabernet, a 2006 All-America Selections winner, produces glossy, deep purple-black, oval fruit on a vigorous, high-yielding hybrid plant that holds up well to the heat and disease pressure of a long Gulf South growing season. Its strong vigor and heavy fruit set make it a reliable choice compared with some older open-pollinated eggplant varieties that struggle in extended summer heat. Harvest fruit while the skin is still glossy and taut, before seeds inside begin to harden, and pick regularly to keep the plant setting new fruit through the season.

common_name: Little Fingers Eggplant (AAS-Winning Slender Asian-Type Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once soil and air have warmed; Little Fingers, a 1985 All-America Selections winner, is a slender, finger-sized Asian-type eggplant well suited to container growing.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 60°F. Little Fingers, a 1985 All-America Selections winner, produces clusters of slender, finger-sized, deep purple Asian-type eggplant fruit that mature quickly and prolifically, giving a much faster and heavier harvest than large-fruited standard eggplant types. Its compact plant size and quick maturity make it a good fit for containers, small raised beds, or gardeners wanting an early eggplant harvest. Pick fruit young while still glossy and tender, several inches long, since Asian-type eggplant quickly becomes seedy and bitter if left to overmature, and harvest often to keep clusters coming through the season.

common_name: Willow Leaf Lima Bean (Heat-Tolerant Heirloom Pole Lima)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed well past frost danger, since lima beans are especially sensitive to cold, wet soil; Willow Leaf is an old heirloom pole lima named for its narrow, willow-shaped leaves and valued for continuing to set pods through summer heat that stalls many other beans.

directions: Direct sow seed an inch deep in warm, well-drained soil in full sun once the soil has thoroughly warmed, providing a sturdy trellis or pole for the vigorous climbing vines. Willow Leaf lima bean is a Southern heirloom named for its distinctively narrow, willow-shaped leaflets, quite different from the broader foliage of most lima beans, and is prized for continuing to flower and set pods through the intense heat of a Gulf South summer that causes many other lima varieties to drop blossoms and stall production. Harvest pods once well-filled but still bright green for fresh shelling, or let them dry fully on the vine for storage beans. Regular picking of mature pods encourages the vine to keep flowering and setting new pods through the long growing season.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after soil has thoroughly warmed and frost danger has passed; Planters Jumbo is a 1930s commercial-standard cantaloupe that was widely grown across the South before modern hybrid melons became dominant.

directions: Direct sow seed in hills of two to three plants in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once soil has thoroughly warmed. Planters Jumbo is an heirloom cantaloupe dating to the 1930s, once a standard commercial variety grown widely across the South before modern hybrid melons largely replaced older open-pollinated types, prized for heavily netted rind and sweet, aromatic salmon-orange flesh. The vigorous, sprawling vines need plenty of room to run and benefit from consistent moisture during fruit development, tapering off as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate sugars. Harvest when the melon slips easily from the vine at full slip, with a strong, sweet aroma at the blossom end signaling peak ripeness.
